subtopics.title: Identify angle types and pairs
subtopics.exposition: An angle is formed when two straight lines meet at a point, which is also known as a vertex. An acute angle is an angle greater than 0° and less than 90°. A right angle is an angle equal to 90°. An obtuse angle is an angle greater than 90° and less than 180°. A straight angle is an angle equal to 180°. A reflex angle is an angle greater than 180° and less than 360°. Adjacent angles are angles that share a vertex and a common side. Vertically opposite angles are angles opposite each other when two lines intersect. Supplementary angles are two angles that add up to 180°. Complementary angles are two angles that add up to 90°. A revolution is the sum of all angles around a point. Two lines intersect if they cross each other at a point. A transversal line intersects two or more parallel lines. Interior angles are angles that lie in between the parallel lines; interior means inside. Exterior angles are angles that lie outside the parallel lines; exterior means outside. Corresponding angles are angles on the same side of the lines and the same side of the transversal. Co-interior angles are angles that lie in between the lines and on the same side of the transversal. Alternate interior angles are interior angles that lie inside the lines and on opposite sides of the transversal. The angles around a point (a revolution) add up to 360°; for the four angles formed by two intersecting lines, â + b̂ + ĉ + d̂ = 360°. An angle is labelled with a caret on a letter, for example B̂. An angle can also be labelled according to the line segments that make up the angle, for example CB̂A or AB̂C. The symbol ∠ is a short way of writing 'angle' in geometry. Angles are measured in degrees, denoted by the symbol °, a small circle raised above the text, similar to an exponent. EF written for lines means the line through points E and F. The notation EF with an overline (\overline{EF}) means the line segment from point E to point F.

subtopics.title: Calculate angles with parallel lines
subtopics.exposition: Vertically opposite angles share a vertex and are equal. Adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary. If the lines are parallel, the corresponding angles formed by a transversal are equal. If the lines are parallel, co-interior angles are supplementary (they add up to 180°). If the lines are parallel, the alternate interior angles are equal. To find unknown angles in a diagram with parallel lines, use the properties of parallel lines to find all equal angles, then redraw the diagram and mark all the equal angles. Start the working by stating the given information with the reason 'given', for example AB ∥ CD (given); every following line of working then carries its reason in brackets. To find an angle that is an alternate angle to a known angle, set it equal and give the reason 'alt ∠s; AB ∥ CD', for example x̂ = 60°. To find an angle that is co-interior to a known angle, write that the two add up to 180° with the reason 'co-int ∠s; AB ∥ CD', then solve, for example ŷ + 160° = 180° so ŷ = 20°. To find an angle that is vertically opposite a known angle, set the two equal and give the reason 'vertopp ∠s =', for example p̂ = ŷ. To find an angle that corresponds to a known angle, set the two equal and give the reason 'corresp ∠s; AB ∥ CD', for example r̂ = 160°. To find an angle that lies with other angles on a straight line, write that the angles add up to 180° with the reason '∠s on a str line', then solve, for example ŝ + x̂ + 90° = 180° so ŝ = 30°. Parallel lines are denoted in a diagram by arrow symbols. In writing, two vertical lines (∥) are used to indicate that two lines are parallel.

subtopics.title: Determine whether lines are parallel
subtopics.exposition: Parallel lines are always the same distance apart. If two lines are intersected by a transversal such that corresponding angles are equal, then the two lines are parallel. If two lines are intersected by a transversal such that alternate interior angles are equal, then the two lines are parallel. If two lines are intersected by a transversal such that co-interior angles are supplementary, then the two lines are parallel. To test whether two lines are parallel, suppose they are, so that a pair of corresponding angles would be equal, and compare the sizes of those angles. If the corresponding angles that would be equal for parallel lines are not equal (here p̂ = 20° but ŝ = 30°), conclude that the lines are not parallel (EF is not parallel to CG).
